title: CppCon 2019: Chandler Carruth “There Are No Zero-cost Abstractions”
summary: Chandler Carruth argues in a CppCon 2019 talk that C++ has no truly zero-cost abstractions. Using examples like unique_ptr, ABI constraints and compile-time costs, he shows that abstractions cost runtime, compile time or human effort.
why: HN commenters cite it whenever zero-cost abstraction claims come up, especially for why unique_ptr is not free on some ABIs.

categories.name: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages

quote.text: Chandler presents his point clearly and goes deep enough into the subject.
